title: You read that verse and quietly excused yourself.
paragraphs: You read that verse and quietly excused yourself.
“Ah, Lord God! Behold, I do not know how to speak, for I am only a youth.” — Book of Jeremiah 1:6
It sounds humble. Honest. Even reasonable.
But if you’re paying attention… it’s something else.

Because that line?
You’ve said it too.

Not out loud, maybe.
But in the moments God nudged you and you froze…

When you felt that pull to speak, to step out, to stop living halfway—and instead you hid behind:
“I’m not ready.”
“I don’t know enough.”
“I’m too young.”
“I’m too late.”
“I’m not that kind of person.”
God saw it.
You knew.
And that’s where this hits harder than you expected.

Jeremiah wasn’t just expressing weakness.
He was resisting a calling.
And here’s what most people don’t realize…

God didn’t comfort his excuse.
He confronted it.
“Do not say, ‘I am only a youth’… for to all to whom I send you, you shall go.” — Jeremiah 1:7
Read that again.
Do not say it.

God didn’t agree with Jeremiah’s self-assessment.
He shut it down.
Because the issue was never Jeremiah’s age.
It was his trust.

You think your limitation disqualifies you.
God sees your hesitation as the real obstacle.
And that’s uncomfortable.

Because it means the thing you’ve been using as a shield…
is actually the thing keeping you stuck.

Jeremiah thought he needed more time.
More growth.
More confidence.
But God had already decided.
“Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, before you were born I set you apart…” — Jeremiah 1:5

Before you existed…
God had intention.
That means your “not ready” doesn’t surprise Him.
It contradicts Him.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior
And this is where it shifts from inspiring… to exposing.

Because if God calls—
and you delay…
That’s not humility.
That’s disobedience dressed in insecurity.

You don’t feel rebellious.
You feel inadequate.

But the result is the same:
You stay silent when you were meant to speak.
You stay hidden when you were meant to stand.
You stay comfortable when you were meant to obey.
And deep down…
You feel it.

That quiet tension.
That conviction you keep pushing away.
God saw it.
You knew.
But here’s the mercy in the middle of it—
God didn’t cancel Jeremiah.
He corrected him… and then equipped him.
“Behold, I have put My words in your mouth.” — Jeremiah 1:9
That’s the part you’ve been missing.
God never calls you based on what you already have.
He calls you based on what He will supply.

You’re afraid you don’t have the words.
God says He is the source.

You’re afraid you’ll fail.
God says obedience is the victory.

You’re afraid of people.
God says, “Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you.” — Jeremiah 1:8
Two voices.

One says: “You’re not ready.”
The other says: “I am with you.”
You can only follow one.
And your life is already showing which one you’ve been listening to.

There’s a version of your future where you keep hesitating,
keep shrinking,
keep explaining away conviction…
And years pass.
Calling buried under comfort.
But there’s another version—
Where you stop arguing with God.
Where you say yes before you feel ready.
Where your weakness becomes the exact place His power shows up.
Because salvation was never about your capability to begin with.
It’s about grace.
“For by grace you have been saved through faith… not a result of works, so that no one may boast.” — Ephesians 2:8–9

The same grace that saves you…
is the grace that sustains your calling.

Not your age.
Not your skill.
Not your confidence.
Grace.
Through Jesus Christ.
And that’s the turning point.
Because this isn’t just about Jeremiah.

It’s about you deciding whether you will keep hiding behind your “I can’t”…
or finally surrender to God’s “I will.”
Say it plainly:
“I’ve been making excuses.”
Let that come out of your own heart.

And if you know someone who keeps saying “I’m not ready”…
you already know why this needs to reach them.
Don’t keep it to yourself.
And if you’re ready to go deeper, to be sharpened, corrected, and discipled beyond surface-level faith…
Because this isn’t about feeling inspired for a moment.
It’s about finally obeying.
